title: Diving into Underwater: Segment Anything Model Guided Underwater Salient Instance Segmentation and A Large-scale Dataset

en.text: On land, asking a model to find the most important objects in a photo and cut out their exact silhouettes is close to routine. Point a camera underwater and everything changes. Water absorbs and scatters light, colors shift, and suspended particles (marine snow) smear across the frame. That degradation trips up even state-of-the-art segmentation models, which is a problem because underwater salient instance segmentation (USIS) is a foundational first step for marine exploration and underwater robotics.

The trouble is not only in the pixels; it is in the data. The field has long lacked a large-scale dataset with pixel-level salient-instance annotations, leaving modern models with little to train on. Meanwhile, foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) show remarkable general-purpose segmentation, but SAM was trained on natural images and does not transfer cleanly underwater. It also expects a human to supply point or box prompts, which directly conflicts with the goal of finding salient objects automatically.

This ICML 2024 paper closes both gaps at once. The authors build USIS10K, the first large-scale underwater salient instance segmentation dataset (10,632 images, pixel-level annotations, 7 categories), and propose USIS-SAM, a SAM architecture reworked for the underwater domain so the model both understands murky scenes and prompts itself. The figure below sets the scene: on the same data, USIS-SAM produces noticeably fewer spurious detections, localization errors, and instance mix-ups than competing methods.

en.caption: Figure 1. USIS-SAM versus recent methods on USIS10K. The line plot (left) reports AP50, AP75, and mAP; USIS-SAM (red) leads throughout. The panels (right) show WaterMask making extra predictions and localization faults and URank+RDPNet showing low precision and instance confusion, while USIS-SAM stays closest to the ground truth (GT). Colors denote distinct salient instances.

Why underwater salient segmentation is hard

Salient instance segmentation asks a model to localize the visually most important objects in an image and separate each one at the pixel level. Underwater, two difficulties compound. The first is imaging degradation: light scattering and absorption produce low contrast and color casts, and marine snow adds noise, so object boundaries blur into the background. The second is data scarcity: prior salient-instance datasets are small and mostly class-agnostic, too limited to train modern large models or to study multi-class underwater saliency in the first place.

Reaching for a foundation model like SAM is the obvious move, but the authors observe that SAM fails underwater on two fronts. Its features are not adapted to the low-contrast marine environment, and it depends on manual foreground prompts that simply do not exist in an automatic salient-segmentation setting. Their reading is that using SAM well in this domain requires two things together: a large-scale dataset that captures the diversity of underwater saliency, and an architecture that teaches SAM to see underwater and to prompt itself. The paper delivers both.
USIS10K: a large-scale underwater dataset

To break the data bottleneck, the authors assemble USIS10K: 10,632 images from a wide range of underwater scenes, each carrying pixel-level salient-instance annotations across seven categories (fish, reefs, plants, ruins, human, robot, seafloor). The examples below pair each original image (left) with its annotation mask (right), where colors mark distinct instances. The set spans clear and turbid conditions and both single-instance and crowded multi-instance scenes.

en.caption: Figure 2. Annotation examples from USIS10K. Each pair shows the original underwater image (left) and its instance mask (right), with colors denoting distinct salient instances. The samples cover a range of water conditions and single- and multi-instance scenes.

en.text: The authors also analyze the dataset to characterize underwater saliency. The next figure summarizes three views: (a) the number of salient instances per category, where fish and reefs dominate; (b) the distribution of salient instances per image, compared against the land-based SIS10K; and (c) global and local color contrast for USIS10K versus SIS10K. Panel (c) is worth pausing on: underwater imagery has systematically lower color contrast, which quantifies the intuition that the underwater setting is genuinely harder.

en.text: USIS-SAM: seeing underwater and prompting itself

USIS-SAM keeps SAM's powerful pretrained backbone frozen and adds two lightweight, targeted modules. The first is the Underwater Adaptive ViT encoder (UA-ViT), which injects underwater domain knowledge into the frozen transformer. The second is the Salient Feature Prompt Generator (SFPG), which replaces SAM's manual point and box prompts by producing salient prompts automatically. The whole network trains end to end. The figure below shows the full framework alongside the internal structure of a UA-ViT block.

en.caption: Figure 6. (a) The USIS-SAM framework: an Underwater Adaptive ViT encoder and a Salient Feature Prompt Generator (SFPG) are added on top of a frozen SAM to output instance masks end to end. (b) The UA-ViT block, where SFFM is the Salient Feature Fusion Module and CA is the Channel Adapter. Flames mark learnable parameters; snowflakes mark frozen ones.

en.text: Start with how UA-ViT learns to see underwater. It injects underwater visual cues into the frozen ViT through adapters: a channel adapter (CA) recalibrates features, and multi-scale convolutions (3×3, 5×5, 7×7) capture structure at different scales, balanced by an average residual that dampens noise. In short, the multi-scale feature is a sum of scaled convolutions over the channel-adapted features, then blended with its own mean by a coefficient lambda before being fed back into the backbone. The strong frozen backbone gains the ability to cope with murky marine scenes while adding only a small number of parameters.

Now the prompting side. The SFPG centers on a Salient Feature Fusion Module (SFFM) that aggregates features from each UA-ViT block, generates salient prompt embeddings automatically, and passes them to SAM's mask decoder. The point is to remove the human from the loop: SFPG turns SAM from a model that waits for someone to click into one that works out of the box on salient targets. Training uses a combined loss covering region proposals (RPN), classification, box regression, and mask segmentation.

What does SFPG actually do? The figure below visualizes the features it generates. Comparing the without-SFPG and with-SFPG columns, adding SFPG concentrates the network's attention on the salient instances (the manta ray, the diver, the sculpture) while suppressing background response. This suggests SFPG does more than fuse features; it also steers attention toward the salient regions.

en.caption: Figure 7. Visualization of features generated by the SFPG. Left to right: original image, ground truth (GT), feature response without SFPG, and with SFPG. With SFPG, the high responses (warm colors) concentrate on the salient instances while background response is suppressed.

en.text: Results: a new state of the art in both settings

The authors evaluate two settings on USIS10K. The class-agnostic setting only requires localizing and precisely masking salient objects, ignoring category; the harder multi-class setting also requires the correct class. In the class-agnostic setting, USIS-SAM reaches 59.7 mAP, ahead of the best salient method OQTR by 3.1 points, the underwater method WaterMask by 0.7, and the SAM-based RSPrompter by 1.5, with AP50 and AP75 of 81.6 and 67.7. In the harder multi-class setting, USIS-SAM scores 43.1 mAP, widening its lead over the strongest baselines to 4.4 points over WaterMask and 5.1 points over RSPrompter.

en.caption: Table 1. Main results on USIS10K (mAP, %). Class-agnostic baseline scores are derived from the leads the paper reports.

en.text: To check what each module contributes, the authors run ablations, reported on the harder multi-class mAP. Starting from the full model at 43.1: reverting the Underwater Adaptive ViT block to the original ViT block drops performance by 1.6 points (to 41.5), confirming that injecting underwater information through adapters genuinely helps the frozen backbone. Replacing SFPG with a generic Multi-scale Feature Enhancer costs 0.9 points (to 42.2), indicating that SFPG does more than fuse features. Additional controls, such as freezing the image encoder and simplifying the multi-scale convolution, further validate the specific design choices.

en.caption: Table 2. Ablation of the key modules (multi-class mAP, %). Each module contributes a clear gain.
rows: SFPG replaced by Multi-scale Feature Enhancer

en.text: Takeaway and boundaries

The lesson here is plain: moving a powerful foundation model into a hard new domain works best when you also supply the right data and let the model prompt itself. By building USIS10K, the first large-scale underwater salient instance segmentation dataset, and by teaching SAM to see underwater through adapters while generating its own salient prompts, USIS-SAM sets a new state of the art for underwater salient instance segmentation. The authors also report that, retrained on the land-based SIS10K, the model still outperforms prior approaches, suggesting the design is not narrowly overfit to underwater imagery.

It is worth being precise about the conditions behind these numbers: a ViT-H backbone, 24 training epochs, six NVIDIA 3090 GPUs, and evaluation centered on USIS10K (with SIS10K as a generalization check). Broader, larger-scale deployment would need further validation. Encouragingly, both the dataset and the code are publicly released, giving the community a practical starting point for further work on underwater vision.

zh.caption: 图1 USIS-SAM 与多种最新方法在 USIS10K 上的对比。左侧折线给出各方法在 AP50、AP75 与 mAP 上的成绩，USIS-SAM（红色）全程领先；右侧可视化显示，WaterMask 出现多余预测与定位偏差，URank+RDPNet 出现低精度与实例混淆，而 USIS-SAM 的分割结果最接近真值（GT）。不同颜色代表不同的显著实例。

为什么水下显著分割这么难
显著实例分割要求模型在一张图里定位视觉上最重要的物体，并逐像素地把每个实例分开。放到水下，任务被两重困难放大。其一是成像退化：光的散射与吸收造成低对比度和色偏，海雪进一步引入噪声，物体与背景的边界变得模糊。其二是数据匮乏：以往的显著实例数据集规模小、且大多不区分类别，既不足以训练现代大模型，也无法支撑对「多类别水下显著性」的研究。

一个自然的想法是借力 SAM 这样的基础模型。但作者观察到，直接把 SAM 用到水下会在两个层面失效：一是它的特征并未适配浑浊、低对比度的海洋环境；二是它依赖人工前景提示，而在自动显著分割的设定里根本没有人来点这个提示。作者由此给出判断：要在这个领域用好 SAM，必须同时准备两样东西，一个覆盖水下显著性多样性的大规模数据集，以及一个能教会 SAM「看懂水下、并自己出提示」的架构。这篇论文两样都给了。
USIS10K：第一个大规模水下显著实例数据集
为了打破数据瓶颈，作者构建了 USIS10K。它包含 10,632 张来自多样水下场景的图像，每张都配有像素级的显著实例标注，覆盖 fish、reefs、plants、ruins、human、robot、seafloor 共 7 个类别。下图展示了几组标注样例：左侧为原图，右侧为标注掩码，不同颜色对应不同的显著实例，既有单实例，也有多实例、多类别共存的复杂场景。

zh.caption: 图2 USIS10K 中的显著实例标注样例。每组左侧为原始水下图像，右侧为对应的标注掩码，不同颜色代表不同实例。样例涵盖从清晰到浑浊的多种水况，以及单实例与多实例场景。

zh.text: 作者还对数据集做了细致的统计分析，帮助理解水下显著性的分布特点。下图汇总了三个方面：(a) 各类别的显著实例数量，可见 fish 与 reefs 明显占多数；(b) 每张图像包含的显著实例数量分布，并与陆地数据集 SIS10K 对比；(c) USIS10K 与 SIS10K 在全局与局部颜色对比度上的差异。图 (c) 尤其值得注意：水下图像的颜色对比度整体更低，量化地印证了「水下更难」这一直觉。

zh.caption: 图3 USIS10K 的基本特征。(a) 各类别显著实例数量；(b) 每张图像显著实例数量的分布，与 SIS10K 对比；(c) USIS10K 与 SIS10K 在全局/局部颜色对比度上的分布对比，水下数据整体对比度更低。

zh.text: USIS-SAM：教会 SAM 看水下、并自己出提示

USIS-SAM 的设计思路是：冻结 SAM 强大的预训练主干不动，只增加两个轻量但有针对性的模块。第一个是水下自适应 ViT 编码器（Underwater Adaptive ViT，UA-ViT），负责把水下领域知识注入冻结的 Transformer；第二个是显著特征提示生成器（Salient Feature Prompt Generator，SFPG），负责替代 SAM 原本的人工点/框提示，自动产生显著提示。整个网络端到端训练。下图给出了完整框架与 UA-ViT 模块的内部结构。

zh.caption: 图6 (a) USIS-SAM 整体框架：在冻结的 SAM 之上加入水下自适应 ViT 编码器与显著特征提示生成器（SFPG），端到端输出实例掩码；(b) UA-ViT 模块结构，其中 SFFM 为显著特征融合模块，CA 为通道适配器（Channel Adapter）。火焰表示可学习参数，雪花表示冻结参数。

zh.text: 先看 UA-ViT 如何「看懂水下」。它通过适配器（adapter）向冻结的 ViT 注入水下视觉提示：一个通道适配器（CA）对特征做重新校准，多尺度卷积（3×3, 5×5, 7×7）在不同尺度上捕捉结构，再用「平均残差」把多尺度结果平衡起来以抑制噪声。用公式概括，多尺度特征为各尺度卷积在通道适配后特征上的求和，随后与其均值按系数 λ 做加权融合，得到注入主干的自适应特征。这样，冻结的强主干在几乎不增加大量参数的前提下，获得了应对浑浊海洋场景的能力。
再看 SFPG 如何「自己出提示」。它的核心是显著特征融合模块（SFFM），把 UA-ViT 各层的特征聚合起来，自动生成显著提示嵌入（prompt embedding），再送入 SAM 的掩码解码器。这一步的意义在于：它让模型不再依赖人工提示，把 SAM 从「需要有人点一下」变成「开箱即用」地面向显著目标。整个模型用一个组合损失训练，同时覆盖区域候选（RPN）、分类、框回归与掩码分割四部分。
SFPG 到底做了什么？下图把它生成的特征可视化出来。对比「不带 SFPG」与「带 SFPG」两列可以看到，加入 SFPG 后，网络的注意力更集中地聚焦在显著实例上（如蝠鲼、潜水员与雕塑），而背景区域的响应被抑制。这说明 SFPG 不只是简单地融合特征，它还起到了把注意力引向显著区域的作用。

zh.caption: 图7 SFPG 生成特征的可视化。从左到右依次为原图、真值（GT）、不使用 SFPG 与使用 SFPG 的特征响应。加入 SFPG 后，高响应（暖色）更集中在显著实例上，背景响应被抑制。

zh.text: 实验结果：两种设定下均刷新最优

作者在 USIS10K 上评测了两种设定。类别无关（class-agnostic）设定只要求定位并精确分割显著物体、不关心类别；多类别（multi-class）设定则更难，还要判对类别。在类别无关设定下，USIS-SAM 取得 59.7 mAP，超过最好的显著方法 OQTR 3.1 个点、水下方法 WaterMask 0.7 个点、基于 SAM 的 RSPrompter 1.5 个点；其 AP50 与 AP75 分别为 81.6 与 67.7。在更难的多类别设定下，USIS-SAM 达到 43.1 mAP，把领先幅度扩大到相对 WaterMask 4.4 个点、相对 RSPrompter 5.1 个点。

zh.caption: 表1 USIS10K 上的主要结果（mAP，%）。类别无关设定下的基线分数由论文报告的领先幅度反推得到。

zh.text: 为了验证两个模块各自的贡献，作者做了消融实验（结果以更难的多类别 mAP 为准）。从完整模型的 43.1 出发：把水下自适应 ViT 块换回原始 ViT 块，性能下降 1.6 个点（降到 41.5），说明通过适配器注入水下信息确实帮助了冻结主干；把 SFPG 替换为一个通用的多尺度特征增强器（Multi-scale Feature Enhancer），性能下降 0.9 个点（降到 42.2），说明 SFPG 的价值不止于融合特征，还在于把注意力聚焦到显著区域。此外，冻结图像编码器、简化多尺度卷积等对照也进一步验证了具体设计选择的合理性。

zh.caption: 表2 关键模块消融（多类别 mAP，%）。两个模块各自都带来明显收益。
rows: 去掉水下自适应 ViT 编码器
SFPG 替换为多尺度特征增强器

zh.text: 小结与意义
这项工作给出的经验很朴素：把一个强大的基础模型迁移到困难的新领域，最好同时补上「对的数据」和「让它自己出提示」的能力。通过构建 USIS10K，第一个大规模水下显著实例分割数据集，并用适配器教会 SAM 看懂水下、再让它自动生成显著提示，USIS-SAM 在水下显著实例分割上刷新了最优结果。作者还报告，模型在陆地数据集 SIS10K 上重新训练后同样优于既有方法，表明该设计并非只对水下过拟合。
需要如实说明的是，论文的结论建立在特定设定之上：ViT-H 主干、24 个训练轮次、6 张 NVIDIA 3090 GPUs，评测集中在 USIS10K（及作为泛化性验证的 SIS10K）。对更大规模、更多样的真实部署，仍需进一步验证。好在数据集与代码均已公开，为社区继续研究水下视觉提供了一个可用的起点。

en.text: Why underwater salient segmentation is hard

Salient instance segmentation asks a model to localize the visually most important objects in an image and separate each one at the pixel level. Underwater, two difficulties compound. The first is imaging degradation: light scattering and absorption produce low contrast and color casts, and marine snow adds noise, so object boundaries blur into the background. The second is data scarcity: prior salient-instance datasets are small and mostly class-agnostic, too limited to train modern large models or to study multi-class underwater saliency in the first place.

Reaching for a foundation model like SAM is the obvious move, but the authors observe that SAM fails underwater on two fronts. Its features are not adapted to the low-contrast marine environment, and it depends on manual foreground prompts that simply do not exist in an automatic salient-segmentation setting. Their reading is that using SAM well in this domain requires two things together: a large-scale dataset that captures the diversity of underwater saliency, and an architecture that teaches SAM to see underwater and to prompt itself. 显著实例分割要求模型在一张图里定位视觉上最重要的物体，并逐像素地把每个实例分开。放到水下，任务被两重困难放大。其一是成像退化：光的散射与吸收造成低对比度和色偏，海雪进一步引入噪声，物体与背景的边界变得模糊。其二是数据匮乏：以往的显著实例数据集规模小、且大多不区分类别，既不足以训练现代大模型，也无法支撑对「多类别水下显著性」的研究。

zh.text: 在陆地上的照片里，让模型「找出画面里最重要的物体并精确抠出轮廓」已经不算难事。可一旦把镜头沉进海里，情况就完全不同：光线被水吸收和散射，颜色发生偏移，悬浮的颗粒（marine snow，海雪）像雪花一样糊在画面上。这类退化让即便是最先进的分割模型也频频失手，而水下显著实例分割（Underwater Salient Instance Segmentation，USIS）正是海洋探索、水下机器人等任务的第一步。
问题不止在图像本身，还在于数据。这个方向长期缺少一个带像素级标注的大规模显著实例数据集，训练现代模型无米下锅。与此同时，Segment Anything Model（SAM，分割一切模型）这类基础模型展示了惊人的通用分割能力，但它是在自然图像上训练的，直接搬到水下并不好用，而且它需要人工给出点或框提示（prompt），这恰恰与「自动」找显著物体的目标相矛盾。
这篇发表于 ICML 2024 的工作同时补上了这两块短板。作者构建了 USIS10K，第一个大规模水下显著实例分割数据集（10,632 张图像，像素级标注，7 个类别）；并提出 USIS-SAM，一个专为水下场景改造的 SAM 架构，让模型既能「看懂」水下画面，又能自己给自己出提示。下图先给出一个直观印象：在同样的数据上，USIS-SAM 相比多种主流方法明显减少了误检、定位错误和实例混淆。

en.text: Takeaway and boundaries

The lesson here is plain: moving a powerful foundation model into a hard new domain works best when you also supply the right data and let the model prompt itself. By building USIS10K, the first large-scale underwater salient instance segmentation dataset, and by teaching SAM to see underwater through adapters while generating its own salient prompts, USIS-SAM sets a new state of the art for underwater salient instance segmentation. It is worth being precise about the conditions behind these numbers: a ViT-H backbone, 24 training epochs, six NVIDIA 3090 GPUs, and evaluation centered on USIS10K (with SIS10K as a generalization check). Broader, larger-scale deployment would need further validation. Encouragingly, both the dataset and the code are publicly released, giving the community a practical starting point for further work on underwater vision.
